requirements.title: Centralized Multi-Cluster Management and Job Placement
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall manage model jobs across one or more clusters and allow users to either let the system select the target cluster or manually specify a target cluster for customized jobs.
ambiguities: Automatic cluster selection criteria and node allocation algorithms across multiple clusters are not fully detailed.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: The MM will manage jobs on one or more clusters.

requirements.title: Weather FDDA Model Job Setup and Submission
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall allow users to set up and submit Weather FDDA jobs (real-time or off-line) by choosing model types (MM5 or WRF), defining JOBIDs, selecting/creating domains, setting schedules or cycle times, and choosing data sources.
ambiguities: WRF domain creation runtime limitations require further clarification on whether dynamic domain creation is supported.
Default GMOD job configuration parameters and standard executable definitions are marked as TBD.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: This feature allows the user to set up and schedule a model job using the MM's Job-Setup module.

requirements.title: ClimoFDDA Job Setup and Integration
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall integrate GCAT functionalities to allow users to set up ClimoFDDA jobs by defining job parameters, domains, time lines, ensemble options, and post-processing product outputs.
ambiguities: Ensemble hourly vs daily options and coupled application execution on post-processed output require further specification.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to integrate the GCAT functionalities within the MM.

requirements.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job Execution
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall allow users to set up and submit standalone post-processing jobs on existing model output files or output from scheduled/running FDDA jobs, including selecting product types and specifying destination locations.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to only run “post-processing” on an existing model output file.

requirements.title: By-Hand Custom Job Submission
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall accept registration and submission of custom 'by-hand' jobs that run pre-existing user scripts on a specific cluster, given mandatory parameters like script location, start time, and runtime estimates.
ambiguities: The complete interface protocol for 'by-hand' scripts to notify the Model Manager upon completion is not fully specified.

source_references.excerpt: In order to submit a custom job to the MM, the user must first identify the cluster(s), where his/her job should run on.

requirements.title: Job Configuration File Loading and Resubmission
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall support loading existing job configuration files, modifying settings, saving updated configurations, and submitting or re-submitting jobs based on saved configurations.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to load a job configuration into MM from a file.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to retrieve a previous job configuration and to re-run this job

requirements.title: Job Queue Monitoring and Lifecycle Control
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall present a job table to monitor scheduled, running, and past jobs, view detailed status and log files, and allow users and super users to stop, delete, restart, and resume jobs according to their authorization level.
ambiguities: Exact rule for job prioritization in the queue is designated as TBD.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to facilitate monitoring of running jobs, viewing the job queue and viewing jobs that ran in the past.

requirements.title: User Email Notification System
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall support sending email notifications to users upon start, completion, or termination/killing of their submitted jobs.

source_references.excerpt: User can choose to receive email notification upon start, end and termination of the job.

requirements.title: Dual Access via Web-Based GUI and CLI
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall be accessible as a stand-alone application or integrated tool via both a Web-based GUI and a command line interface.

source_references.excerpt: The MM will be accessible from a web-based GUI and a command line tool.

requirements.title: Automation and Enhancement of Operational Backend
requirements.description: The system shall extend existing model back-end frameworks to automate setup, running, monitoring, and node management of model jobs to accommodate increased operational workload and hardware capabilities.

source_references.excerpt: The primary goal of this project is to extend the current model back end system and to automate the setup, running and monitoring of model jobs.

test_cases.title: Verify automatic cluster selection when submitting a job without manual target cluster selection

steps.action: Log into the Model Manager Web GUI as a standard user.
steps.expected_result: The main menu displays options to submit a new job, retrieve saved configurations, or view the job queue.

steps.action: Navigate to 'Submit a new job' -> 'Set up a new model job' -> 'Weather FDDA'.
steps.expected_result: The Weather FDDA configuration interface opens with target cluster option unselected.

steps.action: Configure mandatory parameters including JOBID 'AUTO-CLUSTER-01', model type WRF, and click Submit without picking a cluster.
steps.expected_result: The system accepts the job submission and automatically assigns an available execution cluster.

steps.action: Navigate to the Job Queue table and inspect the details for JOBID 'AUTO-CLUSTER-01'.
steps.expected_result: The job details confirm that the job was assigned to a target cluster selected by the system.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: S/he will submit a job to the MM and the MM will make the decision on what cluster(s) the job will be running.

test_cases.title: Verify manual cluster selection when submitting a customized job

steps.action: Log into the Model Manager Web GUI as a standard user.
steps.expected_result: The main interface is loaded successfully.

steps.action: Select 'Submit a new job' -> 'Set up a new model job' -> 'Weather FDDA'.
steps.expected_result: The job setup form appears, including the cluster selection dropdown/field.

steps.action: Explicitly select target cluster 'Cluster-B' from the available cluster options.
steps.expected_result: Cluster-B is selected and set as the target execution cluster.

steps.action: Fill in JOBID 'MANUAL-CLUSTER-01', complete setup, and click Submit.
steps.expected_result: The job is submitted successfully.

steps.action: Open the job detail view for 'MANUAL-CLUSTER-01' in the job queue.
steps.expected_result: The details indicate that the job is explicitly scheduled and running on 'Cluster-B'.

test_cases.title: Verify standard user lifecycle management on own jobs (Stop, Restart, Resume, Delete)

steps.action: Log in as standard user 'UserA' and navigate to the Job Queue.
steps.expected_result: Running and scheduled jobs owned by UserA are listed.

steps.action: Select active job 'USERA-JOB1' and click Stop.
steps.expected_result: Job status transitions to STOPPED.

steps.action: Select 'USERA-JOB1' and click Resume.
steps.expected_result: Job status transitions back to RUNNING.

steps.action: Select 'USERA-JOB1', click Stop, and then click Restart.
steps.expected_result: Job restarts from initial execution stage.

steps.action: Select completed/stopped job 'USERA-JOB2' and click Delete.
steps.expected_result: Job is removed from the active job queue.

source_references.excerpt: User can stop his/her running job. A “super user” can stop any running job.
